* [[Conflict in Iraq]]:
** US war planes strike a building in [[Fallujah]]. Local sources say the strike killed a family of six, including four children. The U.S. military, however, denies a family was killed and issues a statement saying that "intelligence sources indicate a known [[Abu Musab al-Zarqawi|Zarqawi]] [[propaganda|propagandist]] is passing false reports to the media". (Reuters: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050124022501/http://reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=6556916 1], [https://web.archive.org/web/20050121211244/http://reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=6563061 2])
** In [[Samarra]], two car bombs kill at least eight [[civilians]], including a child, and wound eleven US soldiers. In [[Baghdad]], an adviser to the political party of Iraqi [[Iraq interim government|interim]] [[Prime Minister of Iraq|Prime Minister]] [[Iyad Allawi]] is killed in a [[drive-by shooting]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2004/10/20/twin-samarra-blasts-hit-us-convoy (Al Jazeera)] [http://reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=6560635 (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
** [[CARE International]], a health and water aid agency, announces that it is suspending operations in [[Iraq]]. Its local manager, [[Margaret Hassan]], was abducted yesterday. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3760266.stm (BBC)]
* [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] [[Staff Sergeant]] [[Ivan Frederick]] pleads guilty to conspiracy, dereliction of duty, maltreatment of detainees, assault, and committing an indecent act for his actions in the [[Abu Ghraib prisoner abuse|prisoner abuse scandal]] at the [[Abu Ghraib]] [[Abu Ghraib prison|prison]]. He is the third person to plead guilty in the scandal. [http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/10/20/iraq.main/index.html (CNN)]
* [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Rafiq Hariri]] resigns and says he will leave the government, ending several weeks of conflict between Hariri and the [[Syria]]n-backed [[Politics of Lebanon|President]], [[Émile Lahoud]]. Lahoud's term in office was extended last month, allegedly as a result of pressure from Syria; in response, the [[United Nations Security Council]] passed a resolution condemning foreign interference in Lebanon and demanding the withdrawal of foreign troops. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2004/10/20/lebanese-prime-minister-hariri-resigns (Al Jazeera)] {{webarchive |url=http://web.archive.org/web/20041129093552/http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=182273 |date=29 November 2004}}
* The [[Boston Red Sox]] top the [[New York Yankees|Yankees]] in the [[2004 American League Championship Series|2004 ALCS]], and win the series after [[List of teams to overcome 3–0 series deficits|being down 3-0]], winning four straight games in the greatest comeback [[Major League Baseball postseason|MLB playoffs]] history. The Red Sox continue on to face the [[St. Louis Cardinals]] in [[2004 World Series|the World Series]]. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/recap/_/gameId/241020110 (ESPN)]
* [[Ubuntu (operating system)|Ubuntu]] released its first version of the [[Linux]] [[operating system]], called [[Ubuntu_version_history#0410|Warty Warthog]] (4.10). It is based on the Linux distribution [[Debian]].
